description: Required and optional fields for an ICSNPP modbus_detailed.log record (icsnpp-modbus package) delivered as one Kafka JSON message. Base Zeek's own modbus.log carries only tid, unit, func, pdu_type and exception -- it has no address, quantity, request_values or response_values, four fields this contract reads below, without which the modbus-feature-v1 features that read them could not be computed. modbus_detailed.log is therefore the only source this contract reads.

requiredFields.name: ts
requiredFields.notes: epoch seconds, fractional part allowed; negative rejected; the causal feature engine reads this value UNROUNDED (float64, matching the upstream engine's own `ts`); only the event id's ts_millis component and the archived DateTime64(3) row are millisecond-precision

requiredFields.name: uid
requiredFields.notes: Zeek uid; state identity only per the upstream feature contract's excluded_raw_fields -- not itself a feature

requiredFields.name: tid
requiredFields.notes: Modbus transaction id; keys the pending-TID state used by outstanding_requests_before_event, response_without_request, request_overwrite_same_tid, rtt_valid and rtt_s -- excluded from the feature vector itself as transaction state key only

requiredFields.name: func
requiredFields.notes: Modbus function code; source for the fc_1..fc_6/fc_other one-hot and the read/write ratio features. Bound as a String, not an integer, because ICSNPP emits this field as a name (e.g. "READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS") in some builds and as a bare or 0x-prefixed number in others -- Jackson coerces either JSON shape into a String target, so one field handles both without the parser sniffing which configuration produced the record. ModbusFunctionCode.codeOf resolves the accepted forms: the 21 transcribed upstream names, a bare/hex number, FUNCTION_<n>, and (FC|FUNCTION)_?<n> anywhere in the normalized text; an unresolvable value (including a Zeek `<NAME>_EXCEPTION` or vendor name such as `PROGRAM_484`) is a MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD DLQ rejection, matching the upstream engine, which also raises on an unparseable code

optionalFields.name: request_response
optionalFields.notes: PRIMARY direction source (e.g. "REQUEST"/"RESPONSE"); checked before is_orig below. Neither direction field is unconditionally required -- at least one of request_response or is_orig must be present for a record to be scorable, which is a MAP-stage rule the mapper enforces (an unresolvable direction is a DLQ rejection, never a guess), not something this PARSE-stage contract can express as a single required key

optionalFields.name: network_direction
optionalFields.notes: alternate spelling of request_response emitted by some Zeek/ICSNPP builds; treated identically

optionalFields.name: is_orig
optionalFields.notes: FALLBACK direction source, read only when request_response/network_direction is absent; source for the is_response feature (1=response, i.e. is_orig false; 0=request) once resolved

optionalFields.name: unit
optionalFields.notes: Modbus unit id; part of the sequence_context key (client_ip, server_ip, unit_id) together with the endpoint fields below, excluded from the vector itself as sequence key only. Some Zeek builds emit this field as uint instead of unit; either spelling is accepted

optionalFields.name: uint
optionalFields.notes: alternate spelling of unit id emitted by some Zeek builds; treated identically to unit

optionalFields.name: address
optionalFields.notes: register/coil address; source for address_value, address_present, address_delta_valid and address_delta

optionalFields.name: quantity
optionalFields.notes: register/coil count; source for quantity_value, quantity_present, quantity_delta_valid and quantity_delta

optionalFields.name: matched
optionalFields.notes: response causal-match flag; source for response_matched on a response record, ignored on a request

optionalFields.name: request_values
optionalFields.notes: array of numeric request values; source for request_values_present, request_value_count/min/max/mean

optionalFields.name: response_values
optionalFields.notes: array of numeric response values; source for response_values_present, response_value_count/min/max/mean

optionalFields.name: id_orig_h
optionalFields.notes: CONNECTION-level originator address: identical on a request and on its own response, because id_orig_h/id_resp_h name the connection's endpoints, not this one record's sender/receiver. PRIMARY wire spelling -- this is what ZeekConnEvent and ZeekDnsEvent both bind as required=true, and what this platform's sensor actually emits per the passing conn/dns Testcontainers E2E tests. Part of the sequence_context key, excluded from the vector itself as state/orientation only. The ONLY accepted alias is id.orig_h (Zeek's own native dotted JSON naming) -- source_h below is NOT an alias of this field, it is a separate, per-packet field; see its own notes for the precedence between the two. Deliberately narrower than the upstream research engine's own accepted spelling set, which also recognizes orig_h, client_ip, src_ip and source_ip: this platform's sensor emits only id_orig_h/id.orig_h, so accepting the others would be untested, dead code paths

optionalFields.name: id_resp_h
optionalFields.notes: CONNECTION-level responder address, same reasoning as id_orig_h above: identical on a request and its response. PRIMARY wire spelling. The ONLY accepted alias is id.resp_h -- destination_h below is NOT an alias, it is the separate per-packet field. Deliberately narrower than the upstream's own accepted spelling set for the same reason id_orig_h's notes give

optionalFields.name: id_orig_p
optionalFields.notes: excluded from the vector itself as transport context only

optionalFields.name: id_resp_p
optionalFields.notes: excluded from the vector itself as transport context only

optionalFields.name: source_h
optionalFields.notes: PER-PACKET sender address of THIS record: a request's source_h is its own client, but its response's source_h is the server -- source_h FLIPS between a request and its response, unlike id_orig_h above, which does not. This is a separate field from id_orig_h, never folded into it as an alias (that folding was a defect, fixed 2026-09-23: it made per-packet and connection-level values indistinguishable after binding, which is what let a response's endpoints reach the entity key un-oriented -- see ModbusEventMapper.resolvePerPacketEndpoints). When a record carries both id_orig_h/id_resp_h (complete) and source_h/destination_h (complete), the connection-level pair wins and this one is ignored, matching the upstream research engine's own "Preferred: canonical initiator/responder" precedence. Used only when the connection-level pair is absent or incomplete

optionalFields.name: destination_h
optionalFields.notes: PER-PACKET receiver address of THIS record, same reasoning and same precedence (loses to id_resp_h when both are complete) as source_h above

excludedRawFields.name: exception_code
excludedRawFields.notes: excluded per the upstream feature contract: zero Normal support in the training data

excludedRawFields.name: request_data
excludedRawFields.notes: excluded per the upstream feature contract: raw string, exact byte semantics not proven

excludedRawFields.name: response_data
excludedRawFields.notes: excluded per the upstream feature contract: raw string, exact byte semantics not proven

excludedRawFields.name: request_subfunction_code
excludedRawFields.notes: excluded per the upstream feature contract: zero Normal support in the training data

excludedRawFields.name: response_subfunction_code
excludedRawFields.notes: excluded per the upstream feature contract: zero Normal support in the training data

excludedRawFields.name: mei_type
excludedRawFields.notes: excluded per the upstream feature contract: zero Normal support in the training data

excludedRawFields.name: modbus_detailed_link_id
excludedRawFields.notes: not part of the upstream feature contract's feature_order or excluded_raw_fields list; carried by some Zeek builds but never read

invalidRecordPolicy: Malformed JSON or a missing required field routes to the modbus DLQ topic with a reason code; unknown additive fields are tolerated and ignored.
